  • An action protocol must be applied by schools when the CO2 standard is exceeded.
  • Every classroom must have an air exchanger or purifier, supplied and paid for by the department, within 12 months.

25793:
• This bill strengthens secularism in Québec's public and private schools.
  • It adds rules on uncovered faces, religious symbols, religious accommodations and the quality of teaching.
Part 1 Education Act
  • Specifies that public schools are based on the secularism of the State and equality between women and men.
  • Requires students to keep their faces uncovered in schools, training centres and adult education centres.
  • Also applies this rule to children schooled at home and their parents when using school centre services.
  • Requires anyone providing services to students or in contact with them to keep their face uncovered.
  • Extends the ban on wearing religious symbols to staff of school service centres and certain contract workers.
  • This ban does not apply to employees already in their positions or to contracts already underway.
  • Sets rules for staff requests for religious accommodation that involve an absence from work.
  • Bans certain religious accommodations, including those that would affect the duty to attend school.
  • Requires that services to students and decisions by governing boards and boards of directors be made without religious consideration.
  • Requires school service centre staff to act according to the principle of State secularism.
  • Requires school service centres to adopt a code of ethics for members of governing boards.
  • Bans the use of school and centre premises for religious practices.
  • Bans anyone from using a religious belief to influence decisions made under this act.
  • Requires teachers to submit a teaching plan, to be reviewed each year by the school principal.
  • Creates a committee on the quality of educational services to help school administrations monitor that quality.
  • Gives the minister the power to set the exam schedule and to order a school centre to comply with a law or government rule.
  • Provides that certain decisions by the minister, such as suspending a teaching licence, apply even if the teacher challenges them before the Administrative Tribunal of Québec.
  • Extends the requirement to use only French in written and oral communications with students in French-language centres.
Part 2 Act on Private Education
  • Also requires staff of private institutions not recognized for subsidies to keep their faces uncovered.

  • Require students to respect equality between the sexes and to avoid any bullying or violence, including that linked to racism, sexual orientation or disability.

Part 4 Regulation respecting the standards of ethics and conduct applicable to members of the board of directors of a French-language school service centre
  • Housekeeping amendments related to the new secularism rules.

26675:
• This bill implements several measures from the 25 March 2025 budget: vehicles, child and spousal support, municipal taxation, and the pension plan, among others.
  • It also amends dozens of acts to make related adjustments for consistency.
Part 1 Act respecting the Québec Pension Plan
  • Work is only considered to have been performed in Québec if it was also performed in Canada, for the purpose of calculating pensions.
  • Months during which a person receives a reduced CNESST benefit no longer count in calculating their benefits.
Part 2 Highway Safety Code and Regulation respecting road vehicle registration
  • The vehicle value threshold triggering an additional duty rises from $40,000 to $62,500.
Part 3 Highway Safety Code
  • Electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles lose their exemption from this duty between $40,000 and $75,000 in value.
  • A new additional duty applies specifically to electric and plug-in hybrid vehicles upon registration.
Part 4 Act respecting the Institut de la statistique du Québec
  • Clarifies the rules when the Institute collects information for a public body.
  • Allows more researchers affiliated with public bodies to access information for research purposes.
Part 5 Code of Civil Procedure
  • Changes how the seizable portion of income is calculated for a person who owes child or spousal support.
  • Court-ordered support payments for an adult child can no longer be seized.
Part 6 Act to facilitate the payment of support
  • A person receiving social assistance no longer needs to provide a financial guarantee to collect their support payments.
  • In a state of emergency, the Minister of Finance may adjust fees and advances related to support payments.
Part 7 Tax Administration Act
  • The capital of related businesses now counts in determining whether a business is a “large corporation.”
  • Tax information may be shared with the Minister of Finance, without the person's consent, to analyze economic or budgetary policies.
Part 8 Act respecting insurers
  • Life insurers will be able to obtain information about a deceased person from Revenu Québec and the Directeur de l'état civil, in order to notify beneficiaries of amounts owed.
Part 9 Act respecting municipal taxation
  • Municipalities will no longer be allowed to impose a business tax, except for certain fees charged by business development corporations.
  • Municipalities lose the ability to have a rental value roll.
Part 10 Miscellaneous measures
  • More funding for the Fonds Avenir Mécénat Culture, which supports cultural projects.
  • The fee to consult the land register is revised.
  • The government's debt reduction targets for 2032-2033 and 2037-2038 are increased.

26771:
• This bill merges, abolishes or reorganizes several public bodies and funds to simplify government administration.
  • It also tightens accountability rules for senior officials and eases certain administrative requirements.
Part 1 Act respecting the National Institute of Excellence in Health and Social Services and Act respecting the Institut national de santé publique du Québec
  • These two bodies merge into one, the Institut québécois de santé et de services sociaux.
Part 2 Act respecting the governance of the health and social services system
  • Urgences-santé's board of directors will be made up of the same members as Santé Québec's board.
Part 3 Act respecting Héma-Québec and the Biovigilance Committee
  • Héma-Québec takes over the coordination of organ donations, a role removed from Transplant Québec.
Part 4 Act respecting the Commission d'évaluation de l'enseignement collégial
  • This commission, which evaluated CEGEPs, is abolished.
Part 5 Act establishing the Office Québec-Monde pour la jeunesse
  • This body is dissolved and its activities move to the Ministère des Relations internationales et de la Francophonie.
Part 6 Act respecting the Office franco-québécois pour la jeunesse
  • Its internal organization is revised.
Part 7 Act respecting the Centre de la francophonie des Amériques
  • The Centre continues to exist, but as a non-profit organization rather than a state corporation.
Part 8 Charter of the French language
  • The Minister of the French Language receives new responsibilities related to Canadian francophonie.
Part 9 Act respecting parental insurance
  • The Conseil de gestion de l'assurance parentale is abolished; Retraite Québec now manages this plan and its fund.
Part 10 Act respecting the Department of Finance
  • The minister will have to present a financial plan on fighting climate change during the budget.
  • The government will be able to decide, without a new vote in the Assembly, how to split the surpluses of the Electrification Fund between the Generations Fund and the Transportation Fund.
Part 11 Act respecting the Department of Employment and Social Solidarity
  • This department's Information Technology Fund is abolished, its assets transferred to the government's general fund.
Part 12 Act respecting the Department of Higher Education
  • The Fund for university excellence and performance is also abolished, with the same transfers.
Part 13 Act to combat poverty and social exclusion
  • The Fonds d'aide à l'action communautaire autonome and the Fonds québécois d'initiatives sociales merge into a single fund.
Part 14 Public Service Act
  • The Commission de la fonction publique is abolished; its functions move to the Administrative Labour Tribunal.
  • Santé Québec will provide administrative services to Urgences-santé, and the Administrative Tribunal of Québec will do the same for the Financial Markets Administrative Tribunal.
Part 15 Act respecting the marketing of agricultural products
  • The Régie des marchés agricoles will have fewer vice-presidents and fewer members to decide certain cases.
Part 16 Act respecting the Société de l'assurance automobile du Québec
  • The government will now appoint the SAAQ's vice-presidents and set their salaries.
Part 17 Act respecting Hydro-Québec and other acts respecting state corporations
  • The management of Hydro-Québec's CEO, the Commission de la construction du Québec and other executives will have to be discussed in the National Assembly at least once every four years.
Part 18 Public Administration Act
  • Senior officials (state administrators) will have to act with prudence, diligence and fairness, and complete a two-year probationary period.
  • During this period, the government will be able to dismiss a state administrator who was not already a permanent public servant, with a simple 15-day written notice.
Part 19 Act respecting contracting by public bodies
  • Businesses will no longer have to periodically renew their authorization to contract with the government.
Part 20 Act respecting the Centre d'acquisitions gouvernementales
  • Its contracts will be subject to the same rules as those of government enterprises.
Part 21 Act respecting the Société d'habitation du Québec
  • Housing bureaus will be able to merge, and the government will be able to create new ones for any territory it chooses.
  • Joint management of contributions paid to housing organizations by their beneficiaries comes to an end.
  • In the financial sector and elsewhere, several mandatory reports and documents will be produced less often or will no longer be required.
  • The Autorité des marchés financiers, which oversees financial institutions, will have to make certain data and analyses available online.
  • Technical harmonization changes also affect the acts on sustainable development, the chief forester, and pay equity.
  • Many regulations and orders related to abolished or merged bodies (parental insurance, public service, public contracts) are amended or withdrawn as a result.

  • Permit holders will be able to have other businesses carry out more broadly the manufacturing, bottling and transport of their products.

  • The permit to operate a maple grove for maple syrup production purposes will be valid for a longer period.

  • Removes or eases certain formalities required of businesses in the sector.

  • Eases certain administrative requirements imposed on drivers or businesses.

  • Creates a new type of vehicle, the "certified escort vehicle," to accompany oversized or overweight vehicles.

  • Allows the Minister of Natural Resources and Forests to launch pilot projects to test new forestry standards.

  • Certain Télé-Québec contracts will no longer be subject to the usual public contract award rules.

  • Municipalities will be able to create financial reserves simply by resolution, without further formalities.

• This bill creates two new public safety laws and amends eight other existing laws.
  • It mainly aims to better inform the public about certain sex offenders and to regulate protests.
Part 1 Act respecting the public disclosure of information concerning certain sex offenders at high risk of reoffending
  • Creates this new law, with a committee that decides whether information about certain sex offenders should be made public.
  • This new law requires the Sûreté du Québec and Correctional Services to send the committee information about these offenders.
  • The government will be able to define, through a rule without a new vote in the Assembly, who is a "sex offender" covered by this law.
  • Information made public about an offender will stay posted for a maximum of three years.
  • The offender concerned will be able to challenge the committee's decision before the Administrative Tribunal of Québec, which settles disputes with the government.
  • The Sûreté du Québec will have to release the information as decided by the committee, and update it as needed.
Part 2 Act to promote peace, order and public safety in Québec
  • Creates this new law, which bans protesting within 50 metres of the home of an MNA, a municipal elected official or an elected warden.
  • This new law bans carrying or throwing objects or substances that could injure people or damage property during a protest.
  • It allows a police officer to search a person and their surroundings if they believe the person has such an object, and to seize it.
  • It bans, with some exceptions, publicly displaying an object linked to a group on a list of "entities with criminal intent" created by the Minister of Public Security.
  • It sets out the rules for adding a group to this list.

  • Allows the minister to decide which gendarmerie services can be shared between police forces.
  • It also allows other services to be shared between different police forces.
  • It allows the creation of Indigenous police boards to manage a police force shared by several communities.

  • It allows an Indigenous police board to enter into an agreement with the government to establish or maintain an Indigenous police force in its territory.

  • Changes the rules on the term of office of members of the board of directors of the Bureau de la sécurité privée.

26993:
• This bill simplifies the operating rules of professional orders and gives certain health professionals more power to prescribe or treat.
  • It also reorganizes relations between pharmacists, manufacturers and pharmacy chains.
Part 1 Professional Code
  • Professional orders can adopt certain regulations without the approval of the government or the Office des professions, if they follow its guidelines.
  • The Office des professions, which oversees professional orders, must now approve codes of ethics and certain other regulations instead of the government.
  • The Office des professions now decides which diplomas give access to a professional permit, with the government's approval.
  • The Office des professions must create a common rule for all orders to settle disagreements over professionals' bills.
  • The Office des professions can create rules that apply to one or more orders after consulting them.
  • The Office des professions alone decides the ethics rules for members of orders' boards of directors and can investigate and impose penalties.
  • Orders must list more information on the public list of their members and can add other information by resolution.
  • The minimum number of signatures needed to request a special general meeting of an order's members changes.
  • People holding a psychotherapist permit obtained elsewhere in Canada under the new rules will be able to practise in Québec.
Part 2 Act respecting nurses
  • Nurses will be able to request tests and exams in more situations, not only in public health.
  • They will also be able to prescribe tests, drugs, other substances, products and dressings, according to rules to come.
  • The rule that reserved voting rights at general meetings to section delegates only is removed.
Part 3 Midwives Act
  • Midwives will be able to prescribe and provide contraceptive methods more often.
  • They will be able to screen more broadly for sexually transmitted and blood-borne infections.
  • They will be able to treat these infections in a person without symptoms whose test is positive.
Part 4 Optometry Act
  • Optometrists will be able to prescribe and provide more drugs and give more types of care, with fewer restrictions.
Part 5 Dietitians-nutritionists
  • Their scope of practice is updated and they will be able to perform certain reserved acts without needing a medical prescription.
Part 6 Psychotherapy
  • The Interdisciplinary Advisory Council on the Practice of Psychotherapy ceases operations.
  • Marriage and family therapists will be able to practise psychotherapy without a special permit, like psychologists and doctors.
  • The Office des professions will be able to authorize people in training to perform certain acts reserved for psychotherapists.
Part 7 Agronomists Act
  • The definition of practising the profession of agronomist no longer requires that an act be done for payment to count.
Part 8 Pharmacy Act
  • The government will be able to set the cases where a pharmacist can prescribe or substitute a drug with a product from a company in which they have a financial interest.
Part 9 Act respecting prescription drug insurance
  • A new regulation will allow a drug manufacturer to pay certain benefits to an intermediary, such as a banner or pharmacy chain.
Part 10 Regulation respecting drug manufacturers and wholesalers
  • Manufacturers will also be able to pay these same benefits to a drug wholesaler.
  • Several professional laws (Bar, notaries, land surveyors, denturology, medical imaging technologists, legal aid, Charter of the French Language) receive related adjustments linked to these changes.
  • The bill also contains transitional and final measures for applying these changes.

27827:
• Allows a property owner to sign a voluntary contract to protect the biodiversity of their land.
  • The contract may be entered into with a municipality, an environmental non-profit organization, or an Indigenous nation or community.
  • The contract must be notarized and registered in the land register to be valid.
  • The obligations may last for up to 99 years.
  • The contract must precisely describe the monitoring and evaluation measures planned.
  • The contract must specify the conditions under which it may be amended or terminated.
